To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have constructed an ontology that provides an upper level ontology for simulation and modelling.

we have constructed an ontology, HuPSION, for the simulation of human physiology, which is freely available at http://www.scaifraunhoferde/en/business-researchareas/bioinformatics/downloahtml and http://bishop-scai-fraunhofer-de/scaiview.
we have developed a new ontology for the domain of simulation in the biomedical domain and that it is freely available for the scientific community.
In summary, our research is concerned with
providing a comprehensive, formal, machine-readable and human-interpretable ontology for the VPH domain and related domains.
the development of a comprehensive, formal ontology for the simulation domain, which will be used as an enabler for the development of the Virtual Physiological Rat.

the establishment of a shared semantic framework for the simulation of human physiology and related domains, which will be a major step towards interoperability and reusability of simulation resources.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ontology is not only useful for the biomedical domain but also for other domains, e.g. engineering and environmental science.
the ontology is not yet complete, but is a good starting point for the community to work together and to improve the ontology.
HuPSON can be considered a first step towards an ontology that can be used for the VPH.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HuPSON is the first step towards a comprehensive ontology for biomedical simulation.
HuPSON provides an ontology framework for the simulation domain that is applicable for a wide range of use cases, and is a first step towards a more comprehensive ontology for the simulation domain.
we provide a framework for the annotation and interoperability of models, simulations, and algorithms, and that we provide a basis for semantic technologies to be applied in the VPH domain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the development of a domain-specific ontology is feasible and that such an ontology can be used to facilitate the development of a simulation platform.
the construction and application of ontologies is a highly collaborative process that requires the participation of domain experts, ontology engineers and tool providers.
a shared ontology is a prerequisite for the success of large simulation initiatives.
